title: Mixture of LLP and EM for a visual matrix speller (ERP) dataset from
description: EEG recordings from an online visual matrix speller (P300 ERP) study with twelve healthy participants, comparing three fully unsupervised decoding methods: learning from label proportions (LLP), expectation-maximization (EM), and their combination (MIX). Participants copy-spelled a German sentence in three blocks, one per algorithm, using a modified 6x6 grid extended with visual blanks. The dataset supports research on calibration-free brain-computer interfaces based on event-related potentials.
methods_description: 31-channel EEG recorded at 1000 Hz with BrainAmp DC amplifiers and EasyCap Ag/AgCl electrodes (nose reference). Participants spelled 35 characters in three blocks. Each character involved 68 highlighting events with 250 ms SOA and 100 ms stimulus duration, using two interleaved highlighting sequences that created known target to non-target ratios for unsupervised learning.
